groups.defect: The new `retryCount > 1` branch of the OR in the SMS cleanup deleteMany has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, so the SMS cron deletes EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders too. s_51ce1fbc and s_6fbe394f also point out that it can delete reminders that are already scheduled; s_51ce1fbc says to add `scheduled: false`.

answer.reasoning:
s_4680bb7e, s_51ce1fbc and s_6fbe394f all report the same defect at the same lines. The retryCount branch of the OR has no SMS method filter, so the SMS cron also deletes reminders of other methods. s_51ce1fbc and s_6fbe394f also mention that already-scheduled rows can be deleted, and s_51ce1fbc adds a fix for that. Because the members report more than one point, the merged comment needs to combine them.

s_8701b717 is mainly about the comment above deleteMany, which no longer matches what the query does. That is a documentation defect. It describes the deletion of other methods' rows only to show why the comment is wrong. It suggests adding the SMS filter only conditionally ("If deleting non-SMS reminders is not intended"), as one way to make the code and comment agree. Under the rules, a defect that a suggestion only cites as context or touches inside its proposed fix does not link it to suggestions that report that defect. So s_8701b717 stays unique.

This is a judgment call, though: s_8701b717 does state the cross-method deletion as a fact, which is why one judge grouped all four.
